_about: Corrections to the Wikidata item (`qid`) and English Wikipedia title (`wiki`) that history.bin carries for a polity (Atlas v2, the QID audit of 2026-10-13; docs/atlas-v2-polity-qids.md, docs/atlas-v2-design.md §7 "Phase 4 — as built"). Cliopatria names a Wikidata item (`Wikidata`) and an English Wikipedia article (`Wikipedia`) on every row; build-history.js takes, per series, the pair of the rows covering the most years. Some of those pairs are the wrong item (Han dynasty -> Chauhan, Numidia -> the man Jugurtha). `fixes` replaces one (series, wd, wiki) pair with another at the point build-history.js reads the row; a fix that matches no row stops the build. A fix is written ONLY where the right item is unambiguous from Wikidata's own label, description and dates for the polity's span (`basis`: `title` = Cliopatria's own Wikipedia title for the row is the English sitelink of exactly one item, which is the item named; `label` = Cliopatria's title is unusable (it names the wrong thing, a redirect or a disambiguation page), so the item is the one whose English label or alias is the polity's name, with a polity class and dates that cover the span; the `note` says what else was considered). `allow` lists the polities the check in audit-polity-names.js would otherwise fail, each with the rules that fire (`dates`: the item's dates do not reach 1 July of any year of the span; `class`: the item is not a polity or, for a people, not a people or region) and the reason; an entry whose rule no longer fires, or whose item is no longer the polity's, fails the check, so the list cannot go stale. `doubtful` lists polities whose item passes both rules but is open to question, for the owner; nothing is changed for them. Edit this file, run `audit-polity-names.js --fetch-qids` (network) for any new item, then rebuild history.bin (docs/atlas-v2-build.md step 3).

fixes.note: Cliopatria's row is named “Zhou Dynasty”; Q35216's English label is “Zhou dynasty”, its dates (1046–256 BCE) cover the span, and Cliopatria's other row of this series already carries it (the secondary pair, now the main one). Q307066 (Eastern Zhou, 770–256 BCE) is only the second half.

Cliopatria's title “Han (state)” redirects to the disambiguation page “Han”, so no sitelink answers. Of the items labelled “Han”, only Q1574130 is a state of the Warring States (403–230 BCE) and covers the span; the others are Western Zhou states (to 800 BCE), the Han dynasty (from 206 BCE) and the Cheng Han (304–347 CE).

Cliopatria's title “Jugurtha” is a man (a human). Q102679 is the Kingdom of Numidia, 202–46 BCE, a historical country whose English Wikipedia article is “Numidia” — the polity's name; the only other Numidia item (Q12901244) is the Roman province, with no dates.

Cliopatria's title is “Gojoseon”, the older state (2333–108 BCE) that Wiman Joseon followed. The series is named Wiman Joseon and Q703340 is the item for exactly that state (“Wiman Chosŏn”, alias “Wiman Joseon”), 194–108 BCE, inside the span.
Cliopatria's title “Polotsk” is the city (Q200797, a city of Belarus). The series is the Principality of Polotsk, which has its own item whose label is the polity's name, Q517333 (900–1397).

Cliopatria's title “Kingdom of Lithuania” is a medieval state of 1251–1263. The series is Lithuania 1919–1939: the item for that state is the Republic of Lithuania, Q8272919 (1918–1940), a historical country covering the whole span. Q37, the present-day Lithuania, is dated from 1990 and does not.
Cliopatria's pair is Yugoslavia / the Socialist Federal Republic (1945–1992). The series is named Kingdom of Yugoslavia and Q191077 has exactly that label, a historical country dated 1929–1945.

Cliopatria's title “History of Sumer” is an aspect-of-history article, not a polity. Q35355 is Sumer itself (the other items labelled Sumer are a village, a video game, a journal and a surname), a state and civilization of 5500–1900 BCE covering the span.
Q705904 is the ruling family (a dynasty with no state class); the series is the Seleucid Empire. Q93180 has exactly that label and is a historical country and empire, 311–62 BCE.
Q161205 is the ruling family (a dynasty and tribe); the series is the Safavid Empire. Q18234383 (“Safavid Iran”, alias “Safavid Empire”) is the historical country, 1501–1736.

allow.reason: UNRESOLVED. Cliopatria's row carries the Peloponnesian War (a war, 431–404 BCE) for the Athenian coalition of 323–319 BCE. Wikidata has no polity item for that coalition: the Hellenic League is a disambiguation page and the Lamian War (Q28365, 323–322 BCE) is a war, not a polity. No replacement is unambiguous.

UNRESOLVED. The item is the Chinese Communist Party (a political party); the series is the base areas it governed, 1932–1949. Two items fit parts of the span (the Chinese Soviet Republic, 1931–1937, and the Yan'an Soviet, 1937–1950) and neither covers it. No replacement is unambiguous.

UNRESOLVED. The item is a Wikimedia disambiguation page (Cliopatria's Wikipedia title is the disambiguation page "Gothia"). Wikidata has several Gothias and Gothic regions (the Goths, Oium, Crimean Gothia, the Frankish duchy of 790–1065); which one the series 207–382 draws is a historian's decision.

The item is right (its label is the polity's name and it is Cliopatria's own Wikipedia title). Wikidata dates the Palmyrene Empire 270–273; Cliopatria draws it from 261, when Odaenathus's rule begins to be counted. The dates differ by source convention, not by item.
The item is the Etruscan civilization (Cliopatria's own Wikipedia title is "Etruscan civilization"); Wikidata has no state item for Etruria. The series is the civilization's territory.
The item is Mycenaean Greece, a Bronze Age civilization (Cliopatria's own Wikipedia title); Wikidata has no state item for it. The series is the civilization's territory.
The item is the state of Bhutan; Wikidata dates it from a later statement, and the kingdom of 1920 is the same state.
The item is right: the Free City of Danzig, constituted on 15 November 1920; Cliopatria’s row stands for the whole of 1920.
The item is right: France administered Syria and Lebanon from 1920 (San Remo); the mandate was formally confirmed in 1923.
Cliopatria’s Emirate of Nejd (and Hasa), 1913–1921; Wikidata’s item is the earlier Second Saudi State and no item for the emirate of 1920 could be confirmed. UNRESOLVED.
The item is right; Cliopatria dates its Tangier row from 1912, the zone’s statute is of 1923–1924.

doubtful.note: The item is the United Kingdom of Israel (c. 1049–929 BCE), Cliopatria's own Wikipedia title for the row; the series runs to 701 BCE, and for most of that span the Kingdom of Israel (Samaria, Q230407, 929–719 BCE) is the item whose label is the polity's name. Both are defensible; kept.

The item is the Ngô dynasty (939–965), Cliopatria's own Wikipedia title; the series is Dai Viet 947–1406. Q430309 (Dai Viet, 1054–1400) has the polity's own name and covers most of the span. Kept because Cliopatria's title names the dynasty; the owner may prefer Q430309.

The item is the present-day South Africa (from 1910); Wikidata models the Union of South Africa (1910–1961, Q193619) as a separate item whose label is the polity's name. Both cover 1937–1945; kept as Cliopatria's choice of the continuing state.

The item is the present-day Austria; the First Austrian Republic (Q518101, 1919–1934) and the Federal State of Austria (Q176495, 1934–1938) are separate items. The display-name override already shows the latter's name for 1934–37; the QID stays on the continuing state.

The item is the present-day Hungary; the Kingdom of Hungary of 1920–1946 (Q600018) is a separate item, already the evidence of the display-name override for 1920–43. The QID stays on the continuing state.
The item is the County of Savoy (1003–1416); the series runs to 1539, and the Duchy of Savoy (Q426025, 1416–1860) is the item for the later years. Kept as Cliopatria's title.
The item is the Italian Empire (colonial policies, 1882–1960), Cliopatria's own Wikipedia title; Italian East Africa (Q328478) covers only 1936–41. Kept.
The item is the Jin dynasty (266–420), which includes the Eastern Jin; the series (265–425) is named Western Jin. Cliopatria's own Wikipedia title is "Jin dynasty (266–420)". Kept.
